lines.text: AI agents spend most of their time just waiting, and Google built tools for that.
A normal app starts and keeps running. An agent runs for seconds, then waits for a model, an API or a person.
lines.title: App vs agent

lines.text: Agent Substrate splits an agent's saved state, called an actor, from the machine that runs it, called a worker.
lines.title: Two parts

lines.text: When an agent wakes up, it gets a ready worker and its state is restored. When idle, the state is saved and the worker is freed.
lines.title: Wake and sleep

lines.text: Google says agents resume in under 500 milliseconds.
lines.title: Resume time

lines.text: gVisor adds a safety wall. It catches the agent's requests to the main system and handles them itself.
lines.title: gVisor

lines.text: Both are now donated to the CNCF, so anyone can use and improve them.
lines.title: Takeaways
